articles.title: Quantum World Ventures looks to move the technology beyond the lab
articles.text:
Quantum World Ventures looks to move the technology beyond the lab
The Bengaluru-based startup is developing quantum and AI applications for medical technology while building an education business and exploring longer-term opportunities in security.
When Santosh Talaghatti saw his mother fight cancer, the experience left him with a question that would eventually shape his next venture. Why, at a time when technology can make information available almost instantly, does detecting serious illness still depend on processes that can be slow, complex and difficult to access?
“I must create certain technology which will detect the cancer much earlier,” Talaghatti says.
The idea did not emerge in isolation. Talaghatti had spent years working on digital transformation projects involving government, education and public services. He also describes his work with initiatives associated with former President A P J Abdul Kalam as an important influence on his approach to technology, particularly the idea that complex advances should be understandable and useful to ordinary people.
Instead of building quantum hardware, Bengaluru-based Quantum World Ventures (QWV) is applying quantum computing, artificial intelligence and related technologies to medical technology, education, public safety, and fintech.
The immediate focus
QWV began its quantum work with healthcare. Talaghatti says its research includes AI-assisted medical imaging and edge AI, where some processing takes place close to the device instead of being sent to a remote cloud server.
One project is a diagnostic imaging system intended to work with equipment such as endoscopes, CT and MRI systems. QWV’s website describes research into quantum-assisted imaging, sensing and hybrid quantum-classical AI models. It currently places its MedTech work at Technology Readiness Level 4 to 5. TRL is a scale used to indicate how close a technology is to real-world deployment. Talaghatti places the endoscopy work at TRL 3 to 4.
It is important to understand this because a laboratory prototype is still some distance from a certified medical product. QWV says its development path includes testing, validation, regulatory work and manufacturing readiness.
Talaghatti has also described an adaptive hearing aid that could connect with a mobile phone and use brain-computer interface technology. A BCI is a system that interprets signals from the brain or nervous system to interact with a device. He said the proposed device would combine hearing assistance with noise reduction and links to family members’ phones for monitoring and safety.
There is a wider scientific question around the use of quantum computing in healthcare. A 2025 systematic review in npj Digital Medicine found no consistent evidence that quantum machine-learning methods currently outperform classical approaches in digital health. Of the studies assessed as sufficiently rigorous, only 16 involved realistic quantum hardware or noisy simulations. The evidence points to a field that remains largely experimental rather than one with established clinical advantage.
Market shaped by imports
The commercial opportunity QWV sees is linked partly to the structure of India’s medical-device market. The Competition Commission of India found in a 2024 study that around 80% of medical devices were imported in 2022 and described the diagnostic medical imaging equipment industry as largely import driven.
The same study found a high degree of concentration in parts of the market. Five original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) accounted for about 98% of the CT scanner market and more than 91% of the MRI market. An OEM is the company that designs and manufactures the original equipment.
For QWV, the proposed approach is therefore less about building a quantum computer and more about developing software and device integrations that could work with existing medical systems. Talaghatti notes that much of the commercial opportunity will sit in the application layer, although his estimate that hardware represents 10% and applications 90% is a company view, not an established industry measure.
Education is the second strand
Education became part of the venture because Talaghatti sees a shortage of practical understanding around quantum technology and AI. He describes work involving about 18 universities, including Bengaluru City University and Tumkur University, and Centres of Excellence using existing campus infrastructure.
The courses discussed include quantum computing, quantum mechanics, qubits, circuit design, quantum communication, quantum machine learning and quantum cryptography. A qubit is the basic unit of quantum information. Quantum cryptography is the method of protecting communications using principles of quantum physics.
This emphasis on education also predates QWV. Talaghatti’s earlier work included the Global Classroom initiative, which sought to connect rural students and teachers with wider networks of experts and institutions. He has also described work on a smart village model in Maharashtra. These earlier projects explain why learning and workforce development sit alongside the company’s technology work.
The limits of the promise
QWV has also spoken about using AI and quantum technologies in policing, forensics and public safety. Talaghatti said the company was exploring quantum-based pattern recognition for evidence analysis. Its current website describes research around quantum-safe cryptography, AI-assisted investigation and public-safety analytics.
Talaghatti’s claims contain very large estimates about how quickly quantum systems could recognise patterns in criminal evidence, but it does not provide independent test results to substantiate them. The same caution applies to claims about major reductions in diagnostic time. Talaghatti himself acknowledges that AI outputs in the medical setting would still require human validation.
Funding the transition
Talaghatti said QWV had started with about Rs 1 crore of bootstrap capital and was seeking around $10 million to move its medical technology towards productisation. Those were fundraising targets rather than completed financing. The company’s current website now describes a Rs 100 crore fundraising effort.
The funding question is central because moving from research to a commercial medical device requires engineering, testing, clinical validation, regulatory approval, manufacturing and distribution.
What comes next
India’s National Quantum Mission, approved in April 2023 with an outlay of Rs 6,003.65 crore through 2030-31, is intended to support research, industrial development and applications in quantum computing, communication and sensing.
For QWV, the next test is turning prototypes into reliable, regulated products that can demonstrate a measurable advantage over existing tools. That is particularly important in medical technology, where new systems have to clear technical, clinical and regulatory hurdles before they can reach patients.
“It is not only a technology revolution, it has to be a human revolution,” says Talaghatti, explaining the company’s ambition.

articles.title: Hoy No Circula sabatino: qué autos pueden circular y cuáles descansan el 3 de octubre
articles.text:
Este fin de semana entra nuevamente en vigor el dispositivo del Hoy No Circula sabatino, la medida de control vehicular mediante la cual la Secretaría de Medio Ambiente de la Ciudad de México (SEDEMA) restringe el tráfico para mitigar los índices de polución en la cuenca del Valle de México.
Por esta razón, todo aquel que contemple subirse a su auto deberá examinar detenidamente el último dígito de su matrícula y el engomado de verificación antes de ponerse en marcha.
Hay que señalar que el alcance de estas normas no se limita a las 16 alcaldías de la CDMX, sino que impacta de igual forma a diversas zonas metropolitanas colindantes del Estado de México. La reglamentación se encuentra activa en:
- Atizapán de Zaragoza
- Coacalco de Berriozábal
- Cuautitlán
- Cuautitlán Izcalli
- Chalco
- Chicoloapan
- Chimalhuacán
- Ecatepec de Morelos
- Huixquilucan
- Ixtapaluca
- La Paz
- Naucalpan de Juárez
- Nezahualcóyotl
- Nicolás Romero
- Tecámac
- Tlalnepantla de Baz
- Tultitlán
- Valle de Chalco
Asimismo, no olvides que si tu recorrido implica cruzar por alguna de estas jurisdicciones, el Hoy No Circula sabatino te será aplicable de manera obligatoria.
A qué autos y placas afecta el Hoy No Circula sabatino
La finalidad del mecanismo es disminuir el flujo de automóviles para aminorar las emisiones nocivas, contando los sábados con criterios particulares que se integran al sistema ordinario de lunes a viernes. La obligación de reducir el tráfico no afecta a todos los automovilistas simultáneamente cada fin de semana: el distintivo de verificación, el último número de la placa y si la fecha califica como semana par o impar determinan qué unidades se quedan aparcadas y cuáles disponen de vía libre.
Hay que tener en cuenta que el Hoy No Circula sabatino no opera de forma ininterrumpida a lo largo de las 24 horas. Las restricciones estarán activas entre las 05:00 a las 22:00 horas, razón por la cual fuera de esa ventana —durante las horas nocturnas y de madrugada— el tránsito de los coches no se ve afectado, salvo que las autoridades activen una fase de contingencia ambiental o emitan un comunicado extraordinario con medidas complementarias.
En lo referente al 3 de octubre de 2026, el calendario estipula que corresponde al primer sábado del mes, clasificándolo como “semana impar”. Bajo estos lineamientos, los coches identificados con holograma 1 y cuyas matrículas concluyan en cifra impar son los que deberán abstenerse de rodar en las calles mientras dure el periodo operativo.
Si tu unidad coincide con dichas especificaciones, te corresponderá mantenerla resguardada en el garaje hasta superadas las 22:00 horas. Por el contrario, los vehículos que cuenten con holograma 0 y 00 conservan su autorización para transitar libremente bajo los parámetros del Hoy No Circula sabatino. Por su parte, los automóviles con holograma 2 carecen de permiso de circulación en cualquier sábado del año.
Además de las restricciones expuestas, cabe recordar que existe un grupo de vehículos exentos que pueden rodar sin verse condicionados por estos límites. En esta lista se incluyen:
- Vehículos eléctricos, a gas natural o con tecnología híbrida
- Unidades registradas con placas de personas con discapacidad
- Todos los destinados a servicios de transporte público urbano (incluyendo servicios funerarios)
- Los dedicados al transporte escolar o de pasajeros
- Aquellos asignados a seguridad pública y/o protección civil
En caso de incumplir con el Hoy No Circula se castigará con una multa que oscila entre 20 y 30 veces el valor de la Unidad de Medida y Actualización (UMA), una cifra que representa aproximadamente desde 1,924.40 pesos en su escalón más bajo hasta alcanzar los 2,886.60 pesos en el límite superior. Además, el conductor se arriesga a que el automóvil sea trasladado al depósito de vehículos.

articles.title: Discord prépare l’arrivée de davantage de publicités sur sa plateforme
articles.text:
C'est une annonce qui sème la discorde. Plus de publicité, c'est plus de revenus pour la plateforme. Mais les utilisateurs, déjà agacés par certaines nouveautés comme la vérification de l'âge par IA, risquent de ne pas être enchantés par les nouveautés prévues par Discord.
Discord élargit la monétisation de ses services en ouvrant l'accès publicitaire à un plus large éventail d'annonceurs. Jusqu'à présent, seules les grandes marques reconnues pouvaient accéder à ce service, via des accords négociés avec Discord. Maintenant, les petites entreprises peuvent faire leur publicité sur la plateforme.
Un gestionnaire d'annonces en libre-service
Pour démocratiser l'accès à la publicité sur sa plateforme, Discord a développé Discord Ads Manager. Ce nouvel outil centralisé permet aux annonceurs de planifier et suivre leurs campagnes, et d'acheter des espaces publicitaires dans un seul endroit. Si certains annonceurs sélectionnés peuvent déjà l'utiliser, une ouverture en libre-service est prévue dès le début de l'année 2027.
Cette nouveauté est très utile, particulièrement pour les petits studios de jeux vidéo. Les responsables marketing qui n'avaient pas les moyens de négocier directement avec Discord y trouveront également leur compte.
Un nouveau format publicitaire vidéo
La plateforme ajoute également un nouveau format publicitaire appelé Video Quests. Il s'agit de courtes vidéos que les utilisateurs peuvent regarder volontairement en échange de récompenses dans les jeux. Ces vidéos, optimisées pour les appareils mobiles, durent environ 15 secondes et ne semblent, pour l'instant, pas obligatoires.
- Chat vocal, visuel et écrit
- Un outil employé à la fois pour les loisirs et le travail
- L’option la plus populaire
Les marques peuvent acheter des emplacements sur ce nouvel espace publicitaire via Ads Manager. Discord propose également Video Quests Reserve, une version vendue directement aux grandes marques, pour des campagnes d'envergure visant un nombre accru d'utilisateurs.
Des utilisateurs pas enchantés
Forcément, l'expansion des publicités, si elle est intéressante pour les finances de Discord, ne réjouit pas les utilisateurs. Certaines redoutent que l'ajout massif de publicités, ainsi que les technologies de vérification d'âge par intelligence artificielle, finissent par dégrader la plateforme à l'avenir.
Fait notable, Stanislav Vishnevskiy, cofondateur et directeur de la technologie de Discord, a reconnu partager ces préoccupations concernant une possible détérioration progressive du service.
Pour le moment, les publicités sur Discord restent limitées et peu envahissantes, apparaissant sous forme de petites fenêtres et de cartes latérales qui ne s'affichent que sur action de l'utilisateur.

articles.title: CRTC to make it easier to learn about phone coverage availability
articles.text:
The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) has announced plans to improve the information about cellphone coverage that is communicated to the public.
On Friday, the agency said a public consultation has led it to introduce a new approach for how wireless service providers (WSPs) report data on their cellular networks to the CRTC, which is then provided to Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) for its National Broadband Map.
This new standard incorporates three different signal strength thresholds to measure whether WSP connectivity would be of a sufficiently adequate quality to support the following services:
- Level 1: Emergency calls and public alerts
- Level 2: Voice or video calls of at least 3 megabits per second (Mbps) and data upload speeds of at least 1Mbps
- Level 3: Data download speeds of at least 10Mbps and data upload speeds of at least 2Mbps
The CRTC is also setting out other aspects of the standard, including the frequency of when WSPs should report the data, the technology they use to report and the process for providing updates or amendments to coverage. The agency will begin requiring WSPs to report on Level 1 standards in the next Annual Facilities Survey in early 2027, with Level 2 and 3 reporting to be carried out in subsequent surveys.
Building on that, the CRTC will allow Canadians to report locations where the coverage map doesn’t reflect their experience, which should also help improve the accuracy of coverage maps.
With this new approach, the CRTC says Canadians will be able to get more detailed information about coverage in a given area to make it easier to compare service options. Additionally, the regulator says these standards will make it easier for both it and ISED to validate submitted data and generate more accurate coverage maps accordingly.
Source: CRTC

articles.title: Test Ninja Luxe Café Mini : la semi-automatique qui apprend à faire un espresso — Frandroid
articles.text:
Comme beaucoup, je suis passé par à peu près toutes les étapes du café à la maison. La cafetière filtre, puis les capsules Nespresso, puis une De’Longhi Dedica Style à porte-filtre, et aujourd’hui une full automatique De’Longhi Eletta, avec son mode cold brew. J’ai donc une idée assez précise de ce qu’une machine peut, ou ne peut pas, tirer d’un grain de café.
Ninja, la marque de SharkNinja déjà bien installée dans nos cuisines avec ses air fryers et ses blenders, s’attaque au café avec sa gamme Luxe Café. Elle se décline en trois modèles : la Luxe Café Mini, la Luxe Café Premier et la Luxe Café Pro. La marque m’a proposé de tester la plus compacte, la Mini, dans sa version à buse vapeur manuelle. C’est une machine dite semi-automatique, qui mise tout sur l’assistance à la préparation.
Fiche technique
| Ninja Luxe Café Mini (ES301EU) |  | 
|---|---|
| Type | Machine expresso semi-automatique avec broyeur intégré | 
| Broyeur | Meules coniques en acier inoxydable, trémie de 250 g | 
| Assistance | Barista Assist : recommandation de mouture, balance de dosage intégrée, tamper assisté | 
| Chauffe et pompe | Thermoblock, pompe à vibrations | 
| Groupe d’extraction | 53 mm, porte-filtre inox à une sortie | 
| Recettes | Espresso, café crema, café filtre classique, corsé et sur glace (175 ou 235 mL) | 
| Réglages | 3 niveaux d’intensité, 3 niveaux de température | 
| Lait | Buse vapeur inox manuelle (version testée) | 
| Réservoir d’eau | 1,3 L avec filtre à eau intégré | 
| Dimensions et poids | 21,6 × 32 × 31 cm, 8,8 kg | 
| Connectivité | Aucune | 
| Garantie | 2 ans | 
| Prix | 449,99 €, régulièrement autour de 399 € | 
Pourquoi un bon espresso est si difficile à réussir
Un petit détour s’impose avant d’entrer dans le test. Réussir un espresso, c’est faire passer de l’eau chaude sous pression à travers une galette de café moulu, en 25 à 30 secondes. Sur le papier, rien de compliqué. Dans la tasse, plusieurs paramètres dépendent les uns des autres, et il suffit qu’un seul déraille pour rater le résultat.
La mouture d’abord : si elle est trop grossière, l’eau file à travers le café et donne un jus aqueux et acide ; trop fine, elle peine à passer et le café devient amer, presque brûlé. La dose ensuite : quelques dixièmes de gramme d’écart suffisent à déséquilibrer l’extraction. La pression doit tourner autour de 9 bars au niveau de la galette, bien loin des 15 ou 19 bars affichés sur les boîtes, qui mesurent surtout la capacité maximale de la pompe. La température, enfin, doit rester stable entre 90 et 96 °C : un peu trop chaud et les amertumes ressortent, un peu trop froid et le café manque de corps.
À cela s’ajoute l’entretien : purge de la buse vapeur, rinçage du porte-filtre, nettoyage du broyeur, détartrage. Les full automatiques ont conquis les cuisines parce qu’elles gèrent tout cela seules, au prix d’un contrôle limité sur le résultat. Les semi-automatiques comme la Luxe Café Mini visent l’entre-deux : la machine moud, pèse et conseille, l’utilisateur tasse, verrouille et lance l’extraction. On participe, avec beaucoup moins de réglages à deviner.
Déballage et design : petite, mignonne et très soignée
Le carton renferme la machine, le porte-filtre en inox, un panier double, l’entonnoir de mouture, le tamper, un pichet à lait gradué à l’intérieur, un kit d’entretien et la cartouche filtrante du réservoir.
Petite précision, cette version n’est livrée qu’avec le panier double. Pour un usage quotidien, ça ne change pas grand-chose au final.
Une fois sortie de sa boîte, la Mini surprend par son gabarit : 21,6 cm de large pour 31 cm de haut, soit à peine plus qu’une machine à capsules. Pour un appareil qui embarque un broyeur, une balance et une buse vapeur, c’est très bien.
Elle est franchement mignonne et la finition est très soignée, avec des ajustements précis et un tamper qui se range sur le dessus de la machine. Ninja a visiblement pensé une machine qui reste exposée sur le plan de travail plutôt que rangée dans un placard.
Le broyeur est intégré mais séparé du groupe d’extraction : on moud directement dans le porte-filtre, posé sur son support, pendant que la balance pèse la dose en temps réel. Les meules coniques en acier inoxydable sont un choix sérieux. Ce type de broyeur écrase le grain au lieu de le fracasser, ce qui donne une mouture plus homogène et chauffe moins le café que les broyeurs à lames d’entrée de gamme.
Fonctionnement : Barista Assist, une aide qui marche vraiment
Le principe est simple. On choisit sa recette à l’écran, la machine recommande une finesse de mouture, et on tourne soi-même la molette du broyeur pour suivre son conseil avant de lancer la mouture.
La balance intégrée arrête le broyeur au bon poids, ce qui met fin aux dosages approximatifs à la cuillère. On tasse ensuite avec le tamper assisté, qui applique une pression homogène sans forcer, on verrouille le porte-filtre dans le groupe et on lance l’extraction.
Barista Assist prend tout son sens après l’extraction : la machine analyse son déroulé et indique s’il faut affiner ou élargir la mouture. Il m’a fallu trois extractions pour trouver le bon réglage avec mon café du moment. Avec ma Dedica et un moulin séparé, j’avais sacrifié une bonne partie d’un paquet avant d’obtenir un résultat stable. C’est à mes yeux le meilleur argument de la machine, puisqu’elle apprend à faire un espresso au lieu de le faire à votre place.
Une fois réglée, la Mini se montre très régulière : 40 g de boisson à partir de 19 g de café, en une trentaine de secondes. C’est le ratio classique d’un double espresso, environ un pour deux, dans la fenêtre de temps recommandée par les manuels de barista.
Côté rapidité, j’ai chronométré 1 minute et 14 secondes entre l’allumage de la machine et un espresso prêt à boire, mouture, tassage et extraction compris. Mon Eletta, pourtant entièrement automatique, met 1 minute et 40 secondes depuis l’allumage, dont 36 secondes de chauffe et de rinçage. La Mini s’en sort donc bien mieux, grâce à sa chauffe par thermoblock : l’eau est chauffée à la volée dans un circuit compact au lieu d’attendre qu’une chaudière monte en température.
Pas d’application ni de connectivité ici, et je ne vois pas bien ce qu’elles apporteraient : l’écran et la molette suffisent largement à tout piloter.
Performances : le meilleur espresso de ma cuisine
Espresso et ristretto
Je n’avais jamais obtenu un espresso aussi bon avec une machine à la maison. La crema est dense, couleur noisette et persistante, le goût équilibré, sans l’amertume de fond que l’on retrouve souvent sur les full automatiques, qui travaillent avec un dosage et un tassage plus approximatifs. Mon Eletta sert un bon café, mais il n’a pas la concentration ni la texture de ce que sort la Mini. C’est d’ailleurs assez impressionnant de voir toutes les variétés de café qu’on peut tirer d’un même grain.
Le ristretto, plus court et plus concentré, est tout aussi réussi, avec une texture sirupeuse et des arômes bien ronds. C’est l’exercice le plus exigeant pour une machine, puisqu’il pardonne encore moins les erreurs de mouture, et la précision de la pesée fait ici la différence.
Café crema et café filtre
Le café crema, plus allongé que l’espresso mais toujours extrait sous pression, est convaincant : une boisson longue qui garde du corps et une belle mousse.
Le café filtre est bon sans plus. Il est obtenu par une infusion à basse pression dans le même porte-filtre, ce qui dépanne sans égaler une vraie cafetière filtre ou une méthode douce. La contenance plafonne surtout à 235 mL par tasse : suffisant pour un mug, trop juste pour servir toute la tablée.
Lait et cappuccino
La version testée est équipée d’une buse vapeur manuelle, et la machine redevient ici exigeante. Un cappuccino demande de l’attention : préchauffer, positionner le pichet, incorporer l’air en gardant la buse juste sous la surface, faire tourner le lait pour créer un tourbillon, puis couper la vapeur au bon moment. Hé oui… le résultat dépend entièrement du geste. Mes premiers essais ont été ratés, enfin irréguliers plutôt, avec une mousse tantôt trop aérée, tantôt trop liquide.
L’avantage du manuel, c’est le contrôle : une fois le geste acquis, on règle la texture à sa guise, de la micro-mousse brillante pour s’initier au latte art à la mousse épaisse du cappuccino traditionnel. La machine ne prépare pas le café et le lait en même temps, il faut basculer de l’extraction à la vapeur. Enfin, la buse doit être purgée et essuyée tout de suite après usage, sinon le lait sèche et s’accroche au métal.
Entretien et contraintes au quotidien
La Mini reste une machine manuelle : il faut moudre, tasser, verrouiller le porte-filtre, puis le vider et le rincer après chaque café. L’enchaînement n’est pas long et devient vite un réflexe, mais une full automatique vous épargne ce rituel. Il faut aimer le faire, ou apprendre à l’aimer.
La compacité se paie aussi en autonomie. Le réservoir de 1,3 L se vide vite dès que l’on enchaîne les boissons lactées, et les purges successives remplissent le bac d’égouttement, qu’il faut vider souvent. Autre limite liée au format, le porte-filtre n’a qu’une seule sortie : malgré le panier double, impossible de servir deux tasses à la fois. Si vous recevez, les cafés sortiront un par un.
Pour le reste, Ninja a bien fait les choses. La machine programme un cycle de nettoyage automatique, prévient quand un détartrage s’impose et propose un backflush, un nettoyage en profondeur du groupe par reflux d’eau sous pression.
Les pièces amovibles, du réservoir aux paniers en passant par le plateau, passent au lave-vaisselle. Pensez simplement à nettoyer régulièrement le broyeur : les huiles du café s’y accumulent, rancissent avec le temps et finissent par altérer le goût.
Prix, disponibilité et concurrence
La Ninja Luxe Café Mini est vendue 449,99 € et se trouve régulièrement autour de 399 € chez les revendeurs spécialisés. Dans la gamme, la Luxe Café Premier (ES601EU), plus imposante, ajoute notamment davantage de recettes et une mousse de lait automatique, tandis que la Luxe Café Pro pousse l’assistance plus loin avec un tamper intégré.
Face à elle, deux concurrentes partagent la même philosophie de semi-automatique assistée avec broyeur intégré : la De’Longhi La Specialista Touch EC9455.M (599 euros) et la Sage Barista Express Impress (699 euros), qui a popularisé le tassage assisté. Toutes deux sont plus encombrantes et généralement plus chères. Sur le créneau de la compacité, la Mini n’a pour l’instant pas vraiment d’équivalent.

articles.title: OpenAI’s Jalapeño ASICs are deployed alongside AMD EPYC ‘Turin’ CPUs as hosts — Hardware VP says Nvidia’s Vera standalone is ‘a little bit behind… on that maturity level’
articles.text:
OpenAI’s Jalapeño ASICs are deployed alongside AMD EPYC ‘Turin’ CPUs as hosts — Hardware VP says Nvidia’s Vera standalone is ‘a little bit behind… on that maturity level’
Hardware VP Robert Ho says the choice to use Turin was “pragmatic.”
OpenAI’s new Jalapeño ASIC is being deployed internally alongside AMD EPYC Turin hosts, each with 1.5TB of memory. SemiAnalysis described the rack-scale deployment of Jalapeño following the reveal of the chip, which we asked Richard Ho, VP and Head of Hardware at OpenAI, about in an interview. Ho told us that the decision to use Turin was “pragmatic,” describing Nvidia’s new Vera CPU as “a little bit behind… on that maturity level.”
“The way we approached that design was really in terms of de-risking and being able to do that design fast. Vera, as a standalone, is a little bit behind on that maturity level. The Turing device is strong. It did what we needed to do, and partly our partners had some experience with it,” Ho told Tom’s Hardware Premium. “For the Jalapeño program, we were trying to make very pragmatic decisions. We wanted to be aggressive on the goals of the performance and the cost, but we didn’t want to take unnecessary risks. That felt like a good design decision that would fit within the parameters of how we make these design decisions."
There are many Arm-based CPUs on the market, many of which are deployed internally at different hyperscalers, such as Google Cloud’s Axiom and AWS’ Graviton, but Vera and Arm’s own AGI have been described as agentic CPUs, purportedly accelerating the complex reasoning involved in agentic loops compared to their x86 counterparts from AMD and Intel. We asked Ho about this dynamic, and why Turin was the right choice given the close working relationship between OpenAI and Nvidia, who responded with the quote above.
Arm has long touted the virtues of the AArch64 ISA compared to x86, going as far as to claim that its own AGI CPU provides more than twice the performance of modern x86 platforms. That claim is based on internal estimates, not real benchmarks, however. The company has been naturally bullish on AGI’s adoption in the market, though even with an impressive $2 billion in commitments, analysts say the market penetration will still be in the low single digits after two years.
With the explosion of server CPU demand this year and evolving agentic workloads, Nvidia has been at the forefront of messaging, comparing its Arm-based Vera to the x86 competition, boldly claiming a 1.8x improvement over a competing AMD Turin chip; a figure that’s extracted from an overall benchmark suite showing Vera just 3% ahead of AMD’s EPYC 9755.
Many semi-custom Arm designs, from Graviton to Azure’s Cobalt, have focused on core density and efficiency for cloud workloads. Vera and AGI are a shift toward messaging against peak performance. In early Vera benchmarks, Nvidia’s CPU looks impressive, though we’ve yet to see the chip in action in a wide variety of workloads, much less benchmarked against AMD’s upcoming Venice CPUs or Intel’s Diamond Rapids.
What’s interesting about OpenAI’s decision to use Turin is that it’s one of Arm’s deployment partners for AGI, as well as among the list of customers “exploring the Vera CPU,” according to Nvidia. OpenAI, other frontier labs, and hyperscalers keep a wide variety of hardware in their fleet. Pairing Jalapeño specifically with Turin came down to reducing risk, with Ho pointing to the maturity of the platform.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Broadly, x86_64 is more mature than AArch64; ARM has been around since the mid-1980’s, though a proper 64-bit extension didn’t arrive until 12 years after it was introduced on x86. And although Arm has worked its way into data centers over the past two decades, there’s still a much deeper x86 foundation reaching back several decades.
It doesn’t seem Ho’s comments were specifically on the delineation between AArch64 and x86, however. Rather, the comments are focused on the dynamic between Turin and Vera, with the latter being Nvidia’s first foray into a custom CPU core for the data center. Although the early benchmarks of Vera are impressive, it nonetheless represented an unnecessary risk for OpenAI’s rack-scale Jalapeño deployment.
Ho’s comments about OpenAI’s partners having experience with Turin expose where the thinking for the hardware team was at, as well. There are some differences in the practicality of servicing the host system between Turin and Vera, most notably the fact that Vera is board-mounted while Turin chips are socketed; swapping chips isn’t common in a server regardless, but it’s easier with Turin.
Given that OpenAI has a fleet of hardware available, it’s possible Jalapeño will be deployed with a different host system in the future, potentially paired with Arm’s AGI or Nvidia’s Vera. For now, however, Turin was the right choice.

articles.title: How a Geophysics student built Cedisaver on YouTube tutorials
articles.text:
Day 1: A geophysics student at the University of Ghana wants a pair of $100 Birkenstocks, but the price tag is out of reach, and affordable lecture clothes are nowhere to be found. Day 500: He teaches himself to code on YouTube, launches a website, and battles the classic chicken-and-egg marketplace dilemma. Day 1000: Cedisaver averages 6,000 monthly users, connects 37 informal vendors, and scales completely bootstrapped. In this edition of Day 1 to 1000, OPEYEMI KAREEM charts the journey of Moriah Adika—from a campus thrift struggle to building Ghana’s digital marketplace for budget-friendly fashion.
Moriah Adika’s journey to founding Cedisaver began with a pair of Birkenstocks. As a senior high school student at Achimota School in Ghana, he noticed that the popular German sandals commanded sticker prices upwards of $100. For students on a tight budget, acquiring a pair meant scouring second-hand markets or relying on personal favours. The challenge of finding affordable, stylish clothing persisted long after he graduated from Achimota.
“When we started university, I realised that even buying clothes for daily lectures wasn’t easy,” Adika says. “There were simply no affordable options.”
As COVID-19 lockdowns shifted consumer habits online, Adika began exploring whether a dedicated digital platform could make budget-friendly clothing accessible. Studying geophysics at the University of Ghana, he lacked a background in software development or coding. Undeterred, he taught himself how to build the site using YouTube tutorials.
In January 2023, while in his final year of university, he officially launched Cedisaver—an online marketplace designed to aggregate affordable clothing.
“We realised that clothing retail across Africa remains highly fragmented,” Adika explains. “To find affordable items, people have to hunt through thrift stalls, navigate open-air markets, or search scattered social media vendors. We set out to consolidate those products onto a single, convenient platform that handles doorstep delivery.”
Day 1: The first customers
Cedisaver launched as a basic web platform while Adika participated in an incubation programme co-hosted by the British Council, Imperial College London, and the University of Ghana. Although the programme offered no direct equity funding, it provided crucial foundational knowledge on startup operations.
“They guided us through the mechanics of building a startup and key pitfalls to avoid,” Adika says. “Even without capital injection, I credit those early lessons for our initial growth.”
His university classmates served as Cedisaver’s first test audience, purchasing footwear through the platform. This organic adoption offered Adika an early blueprint for customer acquisition before he had developed a formal marketing budget or content strategy.
“The network effect became our primary growth engine before we even figured out paid advertising or content creation,” he recalls.
By the time Cedisaver completed its incubation showcase in late 2023, the platform had served 85 paying customers—establishing an early customer base while the business model was still taking shape.
Adika spent the remainder of the year refining the website and expanding the inventory, focusing on listing enough products to understand customer preferences.
Day 500: Solving the two-sided marketplace dilemma
By 2024, Cedisaver boasted a growing catalogue and recurring buyers, but Adika’s attention was temporarily divided. He was completing his mandatory national service as a quality assurance analyst at Ghana’s National Petroleum Authority, travelling across regions to audit fuel facilities.
Upon returning to Cedisaver full-time, he confronted a critical supply-chain bottleneck. The business had initially sourced inventory directly from large importers rather than onboarding independent merchants, fearing that premature vendor onboarding would erode the startup’s thin operational margins.
“Cedisaver needed to become a platform that attracted a critical mass of buyers first, which in turn would entice vendors,” Adika explains.
This dynamic created a classic chicken-and-egg dilemma: buyers needed diverse product options to browse the platform, but vendors required proof of consistent order volume before committing their inventory.
To break the deadlock, Cedisaver became deliberate about its listings, prioritising everyday apparel and high-demand items capable of rapid turnover.
“Some vendors were initially hesitant about our approach,” Adika notes. “They weren’t ready to formally onboard until they saw steady orders coming through.”
That friction reshaped Cedisaver’s go-to-market strategy. Realising the startup needed to demonstrate clear sales velocity to suppliers, Adika pivoted away from trying to scale every feature simultaneously, focusing instead on driving conversion for featured items.
Day 1,000: Proving the marketplace model
By 2025, with steady consumer demand established, Cedisaver began formally onboarding independent merchants. Today, the platform collaborates with 37 informal market vendors alongside digitally native sellers who possess existing social media catalogues.
Cedisaver now averages roughly 6,000 monthly active users, with an average order value of GHS 400 (~$34). Remarkably, the startup has achieved this scale while remaining entirely bootstrapped.
Navigating capital constraints has forced the team to maintain strict fiscal discipline, safeguarding profit margins while nurturing partnerships with informal merchants. Yet, external fundraising remains a secondary goal for Adika.
“While capital is important, it isn’t our immediate priority,” Adika asserts. “We want to ensure our unit economics, operational strategy, and foundation are rock-solid before pursuing investment.”
For now, Cedisaver remains focused on deepening inventory selection for Ghanaian consumers while proving that its marketplace model can deliver sustainable value to both buyers and merchants across the retail ecosystem.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. articles.title: Lista de tareas dentro de WhatsApp: cómo aprovechar los mensajes destacados y la búsqueda por fecha
articles.text:
WhatsApp puede funcionar como un gestor de tareas sin necesidad de instalar aplicaciones adicionales. La clave está en combinar un chat personal, es decir, un espacio donde el usuario se envía mensajes a sí mismo, con dos funciones nativas de la aplicación: los mensajes destacados y la búsqueda por fecha.
El primero actúa como un panel de pendientes activos, mientras que el segundo permite rastrear compromisos anteriores sin necesidad de desplazarse por el historial completo de conversaciones.
Este método resulta útil para quienes buscan organizar su día a día sin depender de herramientas externas como Todoist, ya que aprovecha funciones que la mayoría de los usuarios ya tiene disponibles en su teléfono.
Cómo crear un espacio de trabajo en WhatsApp para organizar tareas
El primer paso consiste en habilitar el chat personal, también conocido como “Tú” dentro de la aplicación. Para acceder a él, hay que abrir WhatsApp, tocar el botón de nuevo chat y seleccionar el propio nombre, que aparece en la parte superior como la opción para enviarse mensajes a uno mismo.
Este chat se convierte en el bloc de notas principal donde se registran tareas, recordatorios y compromisos. Para facilitar el acceso diario, se puede fijar en la parte superior de la lista de conversaciones. Esto se logra manteniendo presionado el chat y tocando el icono de la chincheta.
Una vez creado este espacio, cualquier mensaje que llegue de un contacto con una tarea asignada, o cualquier nota personal que se escriba, puede marcarse como destacado. Esa acción es la que transforma un simple chat en una lista de pendientes funcional.
Mensajes destacados como lista de pendientes activa
El sistema de destacados es el núcleo de este método. Cuando llega un mensaje con un compromiso, o cuando el usuario se escribe una tarea a sí mismo, basta con mantener presionado ese mensaje y tocar el ícono de la estrella en Android, o seleccionar la opción Destacar en iOS.
A partir de ese momento, el mensaje queda disponible en una sección especial dentro de la aplicación. Para consultarla, hay que ir a la pantalla principal de chats y tocar el menú de tres puntos en Android, o entrar a Configuración en el caso de iOS, y seleccionar Mensajes destacados.
Esa pantalla reúne todos los pendientes marcados, sin importar de qué chat provengan. Funciona como un tablero centralizado que evita tener que revisar conversación por conversación para recordar qué quedó pendiente.
Cuando una tarea se completa, el proceso de limpieza es igual de sencillo: se mantiene presionado el mensaje dentro de la lista de destacados y se selecciona la estrella tachada o la opción No destacar. El mensaje desaparece de la lista de pendientes, aunque permanece intacto en el chat original.
Búsqueda por fecha para rastrear compromisos anteriores
La segunda función clave de este método es la búsqueda por fecha, pensada para revisar qué se acordó o qué tarea se anotó en un día específico sin recurrir al desplazamiento manual por el historial de mensajes.
Para usarla, hay que entrar al chat correspondiente, ya sea el personal o el de un grupo de trabajo, y tocar el nombre del contacto o los tres puntos ubicados en la parte superior derecha. Desde ahí se selecciona la opción Buscar.
Dentro de esa función aparece un ícono de calendario junto a la barra de búsqueda. Al tocarlo, se despliega un selector donde se puede elegir el año, el mes y el día exacto que se quiere consultar. WhatsApp traslada automáticamente al punto del chat correspondiente a esa fecha.
Esta herramienta resulta especialmente útil para auditar compromisos laborales o personales que quedaron registrados en conversaciones largas, donde buscar manualmente un mensaje antiguo podría tomar varios minutos.
Recomendaciones para mantener organizada la lista de tareas en WhatsApp
Para que este sistema funcione de manera sostenida, conviene aplicar algunos criterios al momento de escribir y marcar tareas. Usar formato de negritas dentro del chat personal, por ejemplo al escribir una tarea entre asteriscos, ayuda a identificar rápidamente el contenido relevante. Sumar emojis como un pin, un reloj de arena o un tilde permite distinguir el estado de cada pendiente de un vistazo.
También se recomienda ser selectivo con el uso de la estrella: destacar únicamente aquellos mensajes que representan acciones concretas a resolver en las siguientes 24 o 48 horas, y no cualquier mensaje recibido. Esto evita que la lista de destacados se sature con información que no requiere seguimiento inmediato.
Por último, se sugiere revisar la sección de mensajes destacados al final de cada jornada para desmarcar las tareas ya resueltas. Esta limpieza diaria mantiene el panel de pendientes actualizado y evita que se acumulen mensajes que ya perdieron vigencia.

articles.title: Scammers are selling fake Blu-ray drives to PS3 emulation fans
articles.text:
Discs Matter: Scalpers, scammers, and cybercriminals are having a field day as consumer electronics become increasingly difficult to purchase. Even the humble, theoretically ancient Blu-ray disc format is now being exploited by fraudsters. Now, the emulation community is trying to set things straight.
Developers of the RPCS3 PS3 emulator recently shared a warning about the latest fraud attempts targeting PS3 fans in search of a new Blu-ray drive. An unknown number of scammers are now trying to sell "fake" Blu-ray drives that appear to be newer models but use the same, incompatible internals as older drives.
The RPCS3 team said that, as of September 2026, there appears to be an unusually high influx of fake Blu-ray drives being sold through Newegg, AliExpress, and other popular consumer electronics stores. The bogus drives use enclosures and packaging belonging to high-end models, along with spoofed firmware versions, to appear as legitimate, high-quality drives.
The developers shared a link to the Redump Wiki about the powerful OmniDrive firmware, providing a few hints about the fake drives and how users can spot them. Counterfeit products might be hard to spot at a glance, and taking apart the entire drive to examine the PCB may be too impractical. One way to identify fake drives requires the MakeMKV Blu-ray decryption tool, which can distinguish legit drives based on the MT1959 chipset apart from the fake ones.
 – RPCS3 (@rpcs3) September 30, 2026
The MakeMKV-based method might not be foolproof, as some fake drives reported as MT1959-based are turning out to be incompatible nonetheless. Having a modern, capable Blu-ray drive is becoming increasingly important for emulation and Blu-ray enthusiasts, especially after RPCS3 gained the ability to boot and run PS3 games straight from the original disc.
Needless to say, booting PS3 titles from a fake Blu-ray drive will likely result in a dud. The RPCS3 team reported that scammers can sell the counterfeit peripherals at a higher price, allowing them to make a larger profit compared with less capable drives. Users should always purchase their drives from stores that offer buyer-protection programs, so they can return a fake product if they encounter any issues.
The Blu-ray optical disc format is now on life support. Manufacturing is still ongoing, albeit in diminished volumes, and physical media enthusiasts are fighting an uphill battle against Sony's attempt to kill the market for good. As an optical and physical media enthusiast, I will try to keep my 2022 Asus BW-16D1HT internal drive in good shape for as long as I possibly can.

articles.title: Research roundup: 6 cool science stories we almost missed
articles.text:
It’s a regrettable reality that there is never enough time to cover all the interesting scientific stories we come across. So every month, we highlight a handful of the best stories that nearly slipped through the cracks. September’s list includes a tantalizing hint of the elusive dark matter at the LUX-ZEPLIN detector; entangled Z bosons at the Large Hadron Collider; possible use of psychoactive substances in the Late Pleistocene; and an intriguing technical description of a telescope attributed to Galileo.
A hint of dark matter?
Physicists believe dark matter makes up roughly 85 percent of matter in our universe, with the strongest (but not only) candidate being so-called weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs). But directly detecting WIMPs, or other alternative hypothetical dark matter particles, has eluded physicists for decades. We might have our first glimpse, however, courtesy of the LUX-ZEPLIN detector buried deep in a gold mine in South Dakota. Those potentially exciting results were presented in a scientific talk at the 2026 TeV Particle Astrophysics conference in Japan, with a preprint available on the arXiv. (It has been submitted to Physical Review Letters for peer review.)
The announcement came with strong caveats: the signal is just a hint, well below the threshold needed to confirm discovery, and might just be a statistical fluke. Anyone who regularly follows dark matter news knows that past tantalizing anomalies evaporated as more data came in. But the LUX-ZEPLIN team was unable to account for this event and decided to report their result to the broader physics community. They are still collecting data, as is the XENONnT at the Gran Sasso National Laboratory in Italy. And China’s PandaX detector is currently being built.
If it turns out to be a WIMP that struck a xenon nucleus, it’s not what physicists would predict. The event had a higher nuclear recoil energy than expected, which means the detector should have also picked up several lower-energy WIMPs; it did not. That has theoreticians scrambling to come up with alternative models. Perhaps the interaction rate increases with collision energy. Or perhaps WIMPs have an internal structure, like an atom, and only interact if hit hard enough. Or its coupling to ordinary matter could depend on its momentum.
Cornell University physicist N. David Mermin once described quantum entanglement as “the closest thing we have to magic,” since it means that disturbances in one part of the universe can instantly affect distant other parts of the universe, somehow bypassing the cosmic speed-of-light limit. Albert Einstein memorably dubbed it “spooky action at a distance.” Today, entanglement is the foundation for quantum computing and next-generation sensors, among other applications.
Maintaining quantum entanglement is usually a delicate process; any interference can cause entangled particles to decohere quickly. Despite this, in 2023, physicists found evidence of entanglement between pairs of top quarks produced at the Large Hadron Collider’s ATLAS experiment, raising the possibility that large colliders could be used as an investigative tool to study spooky action at a distance. Now ATLAS physicists have observed entanglement in pairs of Z bosons, according to a paper published in the journal Physical Review Letters.
Z bosons are produced when a Higgs boson decays and are themselves extremely short-lived particles, decaying into pairs of electrons and muons. The ATLAS detector precisely tracks those decay patterns. The physicists used that data to reconstruct the angles at which electrons and muons were emitted to infer the spins of the original Z bosons that preceded them. The authors claim that this is the highest-energy example of entanglement observed to date
Dreams of colonizing Mars face many significant obstacles given the harsh conditions (for humans) on the red planet—including housing. Transporting anything from Earth to Mars is costly, and building materials are especially so. That’s why Hong Kong engineers devised a recipe to combine Martian rocks with terrestrial gelatin and yeast, which then hardens into a durable “living” building material on par with cheap concrete, according to a paper published in the journal Chem Circularity.
Co-author Jishen Qiu of The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology drew inspiration from the hardening of freeze-dried fruits, noting that the Martian environment has extremely low temperatures and pressures akin to freeze-drying. The team experimented with various mixtures of sand and glue, the latter made from gelatin and yeast. But it’s a special yeast coated with sticky proteins similar to those mussels use to adhere to rocky surfaces. The gelatin provides scaffolding for the cells to grow, and the sand provides the structure and mass. Qiu et al. tested their concoction in simulated Martian conditions, 3D-printing small domes the size of wine corks.
They found that the mixture freeze-dries after exiting the nozzle, leaving a light, porous foam with a compressive strength of 10 to 12 megapascals. Per the authors, that is strong enough to build a one- or two-story structure on Earth, where gravity is three times stronger than on Mars, so it should be possible to use their material to make much higher structures on the red planet. It’s less energy-intensive than heating and melting Martian rocks or moon dust into bricks, another approach that’s been proposed. And yeast recovered from dismantled structures could be easily recycled to build new ones.
There is ample evidence that humans in many cultures throughout history used various hallucinogenic substances in religious ceremonies or shamanic rituals, at least since the Neolithic period and the advent of farming and fermented alcoholic drinks (like barley beer). That includes not just ancient Egypt but also ancient Greek, Vedic, Maya, Inca, and Aztec cultures. For instance, in 2024, archaeologists found that an ancient Egyptian vase in the shape of the deity Bes showed traces of chemical plant compounds known to produce hallucinations. And in 2022, archaeologists uncovered evidence that an ancient Peruvian people laced the beer served at their feasts with hallucinogens.
Now Griffith University archaeologists have discovered that humans might have been using mind-altering subsances—by sucking and chewing on betel nuts—as early as the Late Pleistocene period some 25,000 years ago, according to a paper published in Science Advances. Betel nut consumption is common in India and the South Pacific, usually by mixing the seed with slaked lime (which releases the psychoactive compounds) and a few other ingredients to make a “quid,” then chewing it. The effects include mild euphoria and high alertness.
The Griffith team discovered two rare early human forager skeletons from the Indonesian island of Sulawesi, concluding that one dated to 25,000 to 16,000 years ago and the other to 7,600–6,300 years ago. Both skeletons had deep rounded grooves in their teeth, apparently caused by constantly sucking on whole betel nuts. By soaking betel nuts in artificial saliva, the authors concluded that this would release enough arecoline to alter brain function, although the psychoactive effects would be milder.
The authors posit that people from that period sucked on betel nuts to relieve tooth pain, given that these populations are known to have had bad teeth and arecoline is a natural analgesic. But the seeds are abrasive and, over time, wore down the foragers’ teeth so much that inner pulp chambers were exposed. “So while this habit may have been a remedy for toothache, years of prolonged nut-sucking eventually caused much worse dental health problems, creating a cycle of continued habitual use,” said co-author Adam Brumm.
Historians generally agree that a German-born eyeglass manufacturer in the Netherlands, Hans Lippershey, invented the first bona fide telescope in the 1590s. Similar instruments made by other inventors soon popped up, and by 1609, people could buy “spyglasses” in local shops in Paris. Within a few months, the phenomenon had spread to Italy and caught the attention of Galileo Galilei, who fashioned his own telescopes to make ground-breaking astronomical observations that helped the Copernican model of the solar system supplant the Ptolemaic worldview that had dominated for centuries.
Galileo swore never to sell any of his telescopes, and he didn’t document any technical analyses of his instruments either; only eight such telescopes survive; none can unequivocally be attributed to the astronomer. But a historian at the University of Limerick in Ireland has uncovered a previously unknown 17th century description of a four-lens telescope attributed to Galileo in a 1666 manuscript written by a Spanish Dominican friar, detailing his findings in a paper published in the journal Annals of Science.
The text in question is De Tellescopiis Stellarum, by Friar Ignacio Muñoz. Author Jose Maria Moreno Madrid was perusing the treatise when he came across the friar’s analysis of the telescope, complete with diagrams and drawings of the instrument. The analysis was specifically requested by the viceroy of New Spain as a test of the friar’s scientific expertise. Muñoz proposed improvements to the Spanish fleet to King Philip IV in hopes of ending his exile to Portuguese India. Muñoz noted in his manuscript that the telescope belonged to the king and was made by Galileo.
According to Madrid, Galileo had presented Philip IV and his wife with one large and two smaller telescopes to curry favor while working on the problem of longitude. So Muñoz’s description could be referring to one of those three telescopes. The first four-lens telescopes appeared around 1643, but if Madrid’s analysis is correct, this would mean the innovation occurred much earlier, in 1630 at the latest, and could be attributed to Galileo. And Muñoz’s 1666 description would be “the most detailed technical analysis of a telescope provenly made” by the Renaissance astronomer.
Peep shows, aka raree shows, were wildly popular in 17th and 18th century Europe as a form of immersive entertainment by traveling showmen. Pictures or objects were mounted inside a box or wooden cabinet and viewed through a small hole or magnifying glass, creating the illusion of depth perception, sometimes illuminated with candles to create special lighting effects. By the 19th century, peep shows had evolved into cosmoramas, collected in galleries housed in urban bazaars across Britain and Ireland. The cosmoramas weren’t just used for entertainment, but also as a real estate marketing tool, according to a paper published in the journal Early Popular Visual Culture.
John Plunkett, a historian at the University of Exeter, was researching the history of cosmoramas and similar visual technology in the UK and Ireland as part of a broader European project. While poring over advertisements and articles in newspaper archives from the 1820s onward, in order to map the emerging use of cosmoramas around the world, he stumbled on a London auctioneer and surveyor, Brooks and Hedger, who were using cosmoramas in the 1830s to market various estate properties for sale, offering views of homes and grounds including “aerial perspectives.”
Their offices were on Old Bond Street, close to the Cosmorama Rooms of Regent Street, so clearly the firm was capitalizing on the current fad. Per Plunkett, producing cosmoramas would have been a costly investment for the firm, requiring an artist to visit each property and create paintings or drawings from different angles, so this strategy was likely reserved for estates and luxury properties. The practice seems to have been abandoned by 1860, but Plunkett likened it to the virtual tours or walkthroughs employed by online real estate listing services like Redfin, Zillow, or Rightmove in the UK.
Jennifer is a senior writer at Ars Technica with a particular focus on where science meets culture, covering everything from physics and related interdisciplinary topics to her favorite films and TV series. Jennifer lives in Baltimore with her spouse, physicist Sean M. Carroll, and their two cats, Ariel and Caliban.

articles.title: Amazon expands ultra-fast delivery service to more than 120 Indian cities
articles.text:
Amazon expands ultra-fast delivery service to more than 120 Indian cities
The service is now available in cities including Amritsar, Abohar, Jalandhar, Ambala, Mangalore, Manipal, Visakhapatnam, Kochi, Changanassery, Bhubaneswar and Karwar, Amazon said in a statement on Friday.
Amazon has expanded its ultra-fast delivery service, Amazon Now, to more than 120 cities across India, doubling its footprint in two weeks as the e-commerce giant steps up its delivery network ahead of the festive season.
The service is now available in cities including Amritsar, Abohar, Jalandhar, Ambala, Mangalore, Manipal, Visakhapatnam, Kochi, Changanassery, Bhubaneswar and Karwar, Amazon said in a statement on Friday.
Amazon Now offers tens of thousands of products, including groceries, fruits and vegetables, frozen food, personal care items, fashion and beauty products, small appliances, and home and kitchen goods. Orders are fulfilled through a network of nearly 800 micro-fulfilment and urban fulfilment centres, the company said.
"We are delighted to take ultra-fast deliveries with Amazon Now to India's hinterland - from Amritsar & Abohar in the north to Kochi & Changanassery in the south - ahead of the Amazon Great Indian Festival. Amazon Now continues to be the fastest-growing ecommerce business unit in Amazon India's history, with orders doubling every quarter.
"This accelerated rollout underscores our commitment to making fast & reliable delivery accessible to customers across the country. We look forward to continuing to scale up and offering the widest selection of products at the fastest delivery speeds this festive season," said Harsh Goyal, Vice President - Everyday Essentials, Amazon India.
Amazon said in September that Amazon Now had crossed $1 billion in annualised gross sales in India based on the previous three-month period. The company plans to expand the service to more than 300 cities and build what it describes as India's largest "delivery-in-minutes" network.
The company said its broader fulfilment network can offer tens of thousands of products within minutes or a few hours, more than one million products through same-day delivery, more than four million the next day and millions more through Prime delivery.
Amazon Now will also offer deals during the Amazon Great Indian Festival, which begins October 8. Amazon said customers can access deals across categories including smartphones, electronics, fashion, beauty and home essentials, while SBI credit and debit card customers can receive a 10 per cent instant discount on eligible transactions. Prime members will be eligible for additional savings of up to 10%.
Customers can check the availability of Amazon Now by looking for the "Now" banner in the Amazon shopping app.

articles.title: 7 cosas apasionantes que debes saber sobre ‘Digger’ con Tom Cruise
articles.text:
A menos que vivas bajo una piedra, lo sabes: Digger con Tom Cruise está a punto de convertirse en una de las películas más comentadas del año. Y razones no faltan. Por un lado, se trata de una actuación del actor que ya despierta desconcierto y fascinación. No solo por su caracterización de un anciano millonario que intenta salvar el mundo por todos los medios a su alcance. También, porque esta obra rara de Alejandro González Iñárritu es tanto una sátira retorcida como una reflexión sobre nuestra época. Todo en medio del humor más incómodo y singular.
Pero además. Digger es mucho más que una excentricidad del director y doble ganador del Oscar y la estrella favorita de Hollywood. Concebida originalmente tras el arrollador éxito de El renacido, la cinta se burla de todo y de todos. En especial, de la cultura de los genios solitarios de nuestra época al estilo Elon Musk, para indagar en algo más complicado. La responsabilidad colectiva sobre el futuro y, en especial, la de los poderosos sobre sus acciones y decisiones. Todo, sin intentar ser sermoneadora (aunque lo es en cierta forma) y más enfocada en reflexionar sobre el bien y el mal contemporáneo.
Todo lo anterior la convierte en una sátira inquietante que ya despertó sorpresa desde sus primeras críticas y que ahora sacude el debate cinematográfico. Pero además, Digger es una de esas obras curiosas que invitan a la discusión no solo por su trama, sino por todas las rarezas que rodean su producción. Como las siguientes 7 que te dejamos a continuación y que deberías conocer antes de ver la película en su estreno en cines.
Un Tom Cruise irreconocible
Quizás recuerdas a Una guerra de película de Ben Stiller en 2008 y cómo Tom Cruise apareció caracterizado de manera irreconocible como Les Grossman. Este, el vulgar, violento y levemente aterrador productor que decidió enfrentar al secuestro de sus estrellas insultando a través de un teléfono móvil. Si esa imagen del actor te impactó, te tenemos buenas noticias: Cruise vuelve por la misma vía para Digger.
Y eso por la transformación física y estética que el actor debe sufrir para encarnar al multimillonario petrolero de setenta y cuatro años, Digger Rockwell. En esta ocasión, el legendario intérprete se somete a un riguroso proceso de caracterización que incluye el uso de prótesis corporales para simular sobrepeso. A la vez, una cabellera completamente canosa y un acento sureño pronunciado. Un cambio de registro radical que el propio Cruise ha catalogado públicamente como el desafío psicológico más grande de su carrera. Lo que podría valerle no solo su papel más asombroso hasta la fecha, sino hasta la ansiada nominación al Óscar.
Una vuelta de tuerca a la sátira social
Digger sorprende por su trama irreverente centrada en una catástrofe ecológica de escala global. Un argumento audaz coescrito por Iñarritu junto a guionistas de la talla de Sabina Berman, Alexander Dinelaris y Nicolás Giacobone. El relato cinematográfico sigue de cerca las andanzas desquiciadas de Rockwell.
Eso después de que sus cuestionables operaciones de perforación profunda en la gélida región de Groenlandia provoquen una colosal fisura en la corteza terrestre. Algo que desata una crisis ambiental valorada en billones de dólares en daños materiales y sociales. Lejos de asumir una postura de sensatez o arrepentimiento ante la negligencia de su corporación, el excéntrico magnate petrolero sufre un severo quiebre mental. Por lo que desarrolla un delirio mesiánico incontrolable, convenciéndose firmemente de que él es la única mente brillante capaz de salvar a la humanidad. Una burla pendenciera y gamberra que hará las delicias de los amantes de la ironía en la pantalla grande.
Una crítica a las élites en ‘Digger’
Uno de los puntos más interesantes de Digger es su tono satírico. También, la ácida crítica hacia las élites corporativas mundiales que impregna cada escena de la producción. Un enfoque narrativo que los críticos especializados de la prensa internacional han comenzado a comparar directamente con obras maestras de la sátira política. Incluso, ya se le compara directamente con Dr. Strangelove de Stanley Kubrick.
De modo que la cinta utiliza el absurdo y el humor negro para dinamitar el preocupante culto a la personalidad de los líderes empresariales contemporáneos. También, para cuestionar la impunidad económica institucional frente al cambio climático global.
Secundarios de lujo para ‘Digger’
Por si todo lo anterior no fuera suficiente, Digger tiene un espectacular y ecléctico reparto secundario. Uno además, que funciona como el contrapeso dramático perfecto ante la desatada interpretación de Cruise en la pantalla grande. Entre las figuras más destacadas de la lista de actores se encuentra el británico Riz Ahmed, quien se encarga de dar vida a Ganesh.
Este, el metódico asesor gubernamental que actúa como la brújula moral del relato. El reparto también incluye al veterano John Goodman en el papel del presionado presidente Compson. A ellos se suman estrellas de renombre como Sandra Hüller, Jesse Plemons y Michael Stuhlbarg, que brindan a la película su especial personalidad.
Una obra de arte para amantes del cine
Como no podía ser de otra forma, Iñarritu regresando a lo grande, filmando en VistaVision. Una decisión estética del director para otorgarle a la comedia una escala monumental mediante el uso de cámaras Beaumont personalizadas y lentes Leica. Detrás de las cámaras, el director se rodeó de colaboradores habituales de la industria.
Lo que incluye al director de fotografía Emmanuel Lubezki, los editores Conor O’Neill y Stephen Mirrione. También al diseñador de prótesis Kazu Hiro. Lo que garantiza que el apartado visual y sonoro de la película posea la factura impecable de las producciones más ambiciosas del cine moderno.
Giros controversiales en una producción única
Digger es compleja por más de un motivo. Y uno de ellos es ser una película narrativamente desafiante que no será sencilla para todo público. Lo que incluye un monumental monólogo filmado en una sola toma. Un recurso estilístico que ya es una marca registrada en la filmografía del director mexicano. Por lo que en su momento más álgido, Digger pone a prueba la paciencia del espectador.
Eso, mientras Cruise ejecuta un discurso ininterrumpido de aproximadamente diez minutos de duración. Uno además, que requirió de una disciplina corporal y mental absoluta. Lo que consolida su firme intención de alcanzar su cuarta nominación histórica a los premios de la Academia de las Artes y las Ciencias Cinematográficas.
Nada es fácil con ‘Digger'
Digger debutó con 52 % de críticas positivas en Rotten Tomatoes. La calificación más baja que cualquier película de Tom Cruise ha recibido en su carrera. Pero la división de opiniones no comenzó en el agregador. Por lo que ya desde sus primeras proyecciones de prensa, hubo debate intenso y divisorio sobre la calidad de la cinta.
Las primeras reacciones de la prensa aplauden la valentía artística de Cruise por salir de su zona de confort. Pero también se burlan de la ínfima calidad de la sátira. Por lo que, por ahora, Digger está en el límite entre películas muy amadas y las que están destinadas a ser odiadas. Inevitable en una obra de semejante envergadura.

articles.title: Nvidia introduces 64GB DGX Spark to throw local AI fans a lifeline amid the RAMpocalypse — new GB10 config starts at $4999 for those who can work with less
articles.text:
Nvidia introduces 64GB DGX Spark to throw local AI fans a lifeline amid the RAMpocalypse — new GB10 config starts at $4999 for those who can work with less
Less memory, lower price, otherwise identical
Nvidia is tailoring its popular DGX Spark platform and the GB10 SoC to better fit the realities of today's AI models and the broader silicon supply crunch. The company is introducing a 64GB version of the Spark that's meant to be more affordable to local AI trailblazers who just don't need 128GB of RAM.
Back when we first began exploring the capabilities of the DGX Spark and similar systems, the general assumption was that lots of RAM would be necessary to hold the most intelligent models one might want to run, and so unified memory systems built around AMD's Strix Halo, Nvidia's GB10, and Apple's M-series chips could all be configured with 128GB of memory or more.
But the AI field moves fast. Highly intelligent dense models like Qwen 3.8 27B can now fit comfortably within 32GB of RAM (albeit with limited context), so the original Spark's 128GB of memory isn't essential for local inference alone. And skyrocketing RAM prices mean that a chip that’s permanently paired with too much costly LPDDR5X is more of a barrier to entry than an asset. So a more affordable Spark with less RAM makes sense for those who need the capabilities and supporting software stack of Nvidia's GB10 Superchip and can live with less memory.
A "more affordable" DGX Spark is of course relative in today's market. 64GB GB10 systems from Acer, Asus, Dell, Gigabyte, HP, and MSI are slated to start at $4999 when they launch on October 23. Given the ever-shifting prices of memory and storage right now, they might not stay there for long. Assuming you can find a 128GB GB10 system in stock, you can expect to pay roughly $7000 to $9000 for one right now, far above even Nvidia's adjusted MSRP.
Memory capacity change aside, 64 GB Sparks will retain the same ConnectX 7 RDMA NIC as their 128 GB stablemates, meaning that they can still be clustered to boost memory capacity and inference performance if a user does eventually outgrow the bounds of 64GB of RAM. The same 20-core Arm CPU complex from the original Spark carries over unchanged, as does the 273 GB/s of shared memory bandwidth for the CPU and GPU.
To help make use of that ConnectX 7 NIC, Nvidia is also making it easier to join Sparks together with a new software tool, the Nvidia Sync Cluster Assistant, that automates the process of yoking those systems together. (Sync is a remote connectivity and management app for the Spark that allows users to use their Spark’s AI horsepower from other Macs and PCs.)
That tool supplements a variety of community-developed utilities that have sprung up over the past year to make clustering a more seamless process, as we used in our experiments with clustering two Dell GB10 systems together earlier this year.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Nvidia is also adding a feature to Sync called Model Launcher that automatically downloads and starts models like the aforementioned Qwen 3.8 27B across one or more systems and links them to the OpenCode browser-based coding agent so that users can start using their local token factories right away for agentic workflows.
The 128GB DGX Spark and Spark-alikes will remain available for those who need space for larger models and for scaling across clusters, or for more memory-hungry local AI work like model fine-tuning, so there’s basically no downside to this addition to the DGX Spark lineup. In today’s volatile market, it’s good to have options, and a 64 GB Spark gives local AI enthusiasts another choice to better fit their budgets and workflows.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
As the Senior Analyst, Graphics at Tom's Hardware, Jeff Kampman covers everything that has to do with graphics cards, gaming performance, and more. From integrated graphics processors to discrete graphics cards to the hyperscale installations powering our AI future, if it's got a GPU in it, Jeff is on it.
